fields.title: Capex Grows Larger Next Year — Cloud's Answer Atop Deficit Cash Flow
fields.html:
Disclosure of Interest: Anthropic has investment and cloud infrastructure relationships with Alphabet/Google. This article is written based solely on official statements and third-party reporting, applying the same evidentiary standard to positive and negative developments.

1. What Happened

On October 12 at Fortune's Women Leaders Summit, Alphabet President and Chief Investment Officer Ruth Porat stated that next year's capex would "increase significantly." The company remains in a compute supply constraint state, and spending on AI infrastructure this year is approximately $200 billion. Q2 capex was $44.9 billion, and free cash flow was reported as negative $5.9 billion. The reporting presents this as a first instance on a quarterly basis. In the same quarter, Google Cloud revenue grew 82% to $24.8 billion (vs. $13.6 billion in the prior year period), and operating profit surged more than threefold to $8.8 billion. Annual capex guidance was raised by $15 billion to a range of $195 billion–$205 billion. Company-wide Q2 revenue was $119.8 billion and operating profit was $40.8 billion.

2. Connection to the 10-Year Thesis

This event touches the heart of Hypothesis 3, namely that "capex is not a fear but a seed-level reinvestment." The test question of this hypothesis is whether incremental capital returns as incremental toll revenue. This quarter is a rare instance where both answers to the question emerged simultaneously. Capital went out first enough to drag cash flow negative. In the same quarter, cloud showed revenue and profit surging together, revealing where that capital is earning money. The numbers of Hypothesis 2 (Cloud+TPU as a second toll revenue) are layered over as evidence for Hypothesis 3.

A passage worth remembering a decade hence is the direction of Porat's answer. She defined now not as a peak but as the middle of infrastructure construction. This is a public commitment from management that the investment cycle is not yet over. If the commitment is correct, the judgment on Hypothesis 3 is determined not by one or two quarters but by years of cloud margin and capital return trajectories. Falsifying conditions (cloud margin improvement stalling, capital return decline persisting for 2 years) have not yet been met either way. However, it is clear that the testing period has lengthened.

The discrepancy between the ledger and latest reporting is also noted. The 2026 capex guidance range in the ledger is lower than the range in latest reporting. The company appears to have raised guidance after the ledger was prepared. This gap itself is evidence that the pressure of Hypothesis 3 is intensifying.

3. Thesis Judgment

Judgment Withheld. Cloud's profit increase is evidence in the direction that reinvestment returns as earnings, and the quarterly free cash flow deficit and next year's additional increase announcement are evidence lengthening the verification period. With both signals growing in opposite directions simultaneously, confidence is neither raised nor lowered.

4. What Could Be Wrong

The opposing view is this: Cloud's high growth could be the result of captured demand amid supply constraints, and there is no guarantee that price and margin will hold after infrastructure scales. Management's "still in construction phase" statement is an explanation for spending increases, while simultaneously being language that does not say when spending will end. Community backlash against data centers under construction is also being reported, so permitting and power could become bottlenecks before earnings. Reading cloud figures as evidence of reinvestment success, as this article does, is interpretation; another reader could read the same figures as temporary demand capture. Moreover, whether this quarter's free cash flow deficit is one-time or a structural shift cannot be resolved with one quarter of data.

Thesis Revision Proposal

The capex guidance range entered in the evidence column of Hypothesis 3 in Logbook v1.0 does not match the latest reporting (revised annual guidance). It is proposed to update the evidence column to the latest range and add the fact of quarterly free cash flow deficit and the statement "capex to increase significantly next year" to the evidence and observation sections. Logbook revision occurs only after director approval.

5. Next Observation Points

  • Q3 earnings scheduled for October 28: Cloud growth rate and operating profit trajectory, whether quarterly free cash flow emerges from negative territory
  • Whether annual capex guidance undergoes further revision and specific commentary on 2027 direction
  • To what extent third-party TPU sales revenue appears as a separate line versus in-house consumption
